# Proximity propagation inside disjunctive layout search

I read both supplied proposals in full: baseline/proposal.md and attempt_00/proposal.md, together with all three supplied score snapshots and their source files. No additional historical proposals or failure logs are supplied.

The baseline and its identical init snapshot measured combined score 0.6738452380952381, support 1.0, collision freedom 0.9583333333333334, relation satisfaction 0.21666666666666667, and zero strict successes. Its code ignores relations and centers every child on its parent; these explain its ordering failures and recurring sibling collisions. Attempt_00 introduced difference constraints, collision branching, and proximity projection. It measured 1.0 combined score and strict success on all six development scenes. This is evidence of success on those scenes, not evidence about unseen configurations. There is no measured failed constraint-solver attempt to repair and no established plateau across repeated variants.

The new mechanism combines that successful graph representation with circular proximity propagation during search. All-pairs difference-constraint closure supplies a necessary minimum separation on each axis. A near disk then bounds the other axis by sqrt(radius squared minus minimum separation squared). These bounds are inserted back into the graphs and propagated again. Thus proximity can constrain packing choices before coordinates are projected, rather than acting only as a post-placement repair. This cross-axis propagation was absent from both historical implementations.

Search prioritizes states satisfying the propagated proximity constraints, branches on collisions with the fewest graph-feasible separating choices, and retains a bounded soft-relation recovery search for contradictory inputs. Dykstra projection remains available for the residual curved constraints. Candidate selection uses the supplied geometric objective and retains room-contained fallbacks.

Expected benefit is earlier rejection of incompatible packing directions and less projection work on narrow proximity constraints. Risks include cubic closure cost, bounded search missing a packing, and slow projection near tangencies. Propagation uses outward numerical slack so its linear bounds are conservative. Work is bounded and uses only the standard library. The submitted code has not been executed or evaluated; no improvement over the observed historical score is claimed.

# Score-aware relaxation of geometric obligations

## Complete supplied history
I reviewed all eight supplied proposal files in full: attempt_00/proposal.md; baseline/proposal.md; and the baseline, attempt_00, and attempt_01 proposals in each historical branch. I also reviewed all eleven supplied source/score pairs, including initialization copies. No error logs were supplied.

All six baseline/init snapshots use identifier-grid placement and parent-centered children. Each reports combined score 0.6738452380952381, strict success 0, support 1.0, collision freedom 0.9583333333333334, and relation satisfaction 0.21666666666666667. Their code ignores relations and places siblings at the same center. These are structural limitations, not an execution failure worth retrying.

Historical explore_b0/attempt_00 introduces difference constraints, collision branching, and angular proximity rectangles; attempt_01 adds continuous disk projection. Historical explore_b1/attempt_00 uses centered graph coordinates, disk projection, and greedy directional subsets; attempt_01 adds cross-axis proximity propagation and constrained-first branching. Each reports combined score and strict success 1.0. Their evaluation times are approximately 0.178, 0.202, 0.201, and 0.206 seconds, respectively. The current sibling attempt_00 adds relation-owner cycle extraction and relation retraction; it also reports combined score and strict success 1.0, at approximately 0.216 seconds. All these observations use analytic AABB evaluation, with Blender verification false. There is no measured failed graph solver to repair, and the repeated outcomes do not establish gains from further geometric refinements.

## New mechanism
Extend conflict-directed search from relation selection to explicit selection of geometric obligations. Give each support-footprint obligation and each collision pair its own owner, alongside relation owners. A positive graph cycle can retract any implicated optional owner. Retracting a support owner removes both horizontal footprint constraints for that object. Retracting a collision owner removes that pair's separating commitment and records a waiver, so later search can resolve other collisions instead of repeatedly branching on an unavoidable pair.

Every unresolved collision offers four separating branches and a fifth waiver branch. Room bounds remain mandatory. Heights remain determined by the immutable support hierarchy, followed by room clamping for best-effort output. All actual support, collisions, and relations are scored from coordinates regardless of which obligations were waived. A waiver is permission to stop enforcing an obligation, not a declaration that it is violated or satisfied.

This is a new combination of the successful graph/conflict machinery with score-aware soft geometry. Previous implementations made support footprints mandatory and kept resolving collisions without an explicit skip-and-continue state. Relation-only retraction cannot explore the same tradeoffs. The change targets cases where accepting one overlap or one unsupported footprint permits many other constraints to be satisfied; it does not repeat proximity projection or propagation.

## Expected benefit and risk
Explicit geometry waivers may improve partial layouts when complete geometric feasibility is impossible or inaccessible within the search budget. They also allow conflicting packing commitments to be removed while continuing useful work elsewhere. The supplied results do not demonstrate this benefit.

Risks include a larger search space, inaccurate heuristic branch priorities, finite angular proximity coverage, and increased runtime. Search has fixed state and expansion limits, uses only the standard library, and scores room-clamped candidates independently of their enforcement state. Impossible object-to-room dimensions cannot be repaired without changing immutable input. This source has not been executed or evaluated; no correctness, runtime, or score improvement is claimed.

dream_g2_online.proposal:
# Contact-event neighborhood repair after joint constraint search

## Complete supplied history
I read all eleven supplied proposal files in full and all fifteen matching source/score pairs. These comprise the top-level baseline, three historical baselines, their four initialization copies, four iter000 attempts, two iter001 attempts, and the current sibling attempt_00. No error logs were supplied.

All eight baseline/init snapshots use identifier-grid placement with parent-centered children. Each reports combined score 0.6738452380952381, strict success 0, support 1.0, collision freedom 0.9583333333333334, and relation satisfaction 0.21666666666666667. Their source ignores relations and gives siblings identical centers. These are structural weaknesses, not failed implementations of the later mechanisms.

Every evolved snapshot reports combined score and strict success 1.0 on the six supplied development scenes. Iter000/explore_b0/00 uses difference constraints, collision branching, and proximity rectangles (approximately 0.178 seconds); /01 adds disk projection (0.202 seconds). Iter000/explore_b1/00 uses centered graph solutions, projection, and greedy relation subsets (0.201 seconds); /01 adds circular bound propagation (0.206 seconds). Iter001/explore_b0/00 adds conflict-directed relation retraction (0.216 seconds); /01 adds support-footprint and collision waivers (0.198 seconds). The current attempt_00 adds joint XYZ search and retractable complete support contacts (0.202 seconds). These are analytic AABB observations, with Blender verification false. There is no observed failed evolved attempt motivating a bug retry.

## New mechanism
Retain joint XYZ conflict search as a first-stage constructor. If its incumbent remains imperfect, switch representations: search directly over rigid translations of individual objects and complete support subtrees. Along one axis, enumerate geometric events where the actual discrete objective can change: room boundaries, collision contact faces, support-footprint boundaries, exact support heights, left-of thresholds, and roots of near-circle intersections with the translation line. Evaluate those event translations against every actual obligation, including obligations previously waived by graph search.

A subtree move preserves relative positions and internal contacts while moving a coordinated assembly. Singleton moves permit repair of an individual contact. A move can simultaneously recover several waived obligations without reconstructing their graph decisions. The repair stage retains only improvements under coordinate-based scoring and uses fixed sweep and candidate budgets. It keeps the graph incumbent if no better candidate is found.

This is a new combination of successful joint constraint search with geometric neighborhood optimization. Previous attempts add constraints, project onto enforced constraints, or monotonically retract obligations. None enumerates direct rigid-subtree translation events against the full objective after graph search. This deliberately explores a different mechanism rather than another proximity-angle or retraction-cost adjustment.

## Expected benefit and risk
The new stage may recover support or relations incidentally lost during bounded graph search, and may move an entire assembly past a local packing obstruction. Supplied measurements establish no improvement for this mechanism. Coordinate-wise event moves can miss coordinated multi-axis rearrangements and moves requiring temporary score degradation. Subtree neighborhoods can be expensive, so candidate evaluations are capped. Floating-point tangencies remain a risk; candidates are clamped to room bounds and assessed independently. Oversized objects cannot be made room-contained without changing immutable dimensions.

Only the standard library is used. No execution, compilation, evaluation, or performance improvement is claimed.

# Conflict-directed relation relaxation

## Complete supplied history
I reviewed all seven supplied proposal files in full: the top-level baseline, both historical baseline copies, and attempts 00 and 01 from both explore_b0 and explore_b1. I also reviewed every supplied source and matching score snapshot. No error logs were supplied.

All baseline/init copies use identifier-grid placement and parent-centered children. They report combined score 0.6738452380952381, strict success 0, support 1.0, collision freedom 0.9583333333333334, and relation satisfaction 0.21666666666666667. The source establishes structural causes: relations are ignored and siblings can share a center.

explore_b0/attempt_00 uses difference constraints, collision branching, and angular proximity rectangles; its measured combined score and strict success are both 1.0. explore_b0/attempt_01 adds continuous disk projection and reports the same outcomes. explore_b1/attempt_00 uses centered graph solutions, disk projection, and several greedy directional subsets; it also reports both outcomes as 1.0. explore_b1/attempt_01 adds cross-axis proximity propagation and constrained-first collision branching, again reporting both as 1.0. Their reported evaluation times are approximately 0.178, 0.202, 0.201, and 0.206 seconds respectively. These are analytic AABB observations, with Blender verification false. None is an observed failed solver requiring a bug retry.

## New mechanism
The successful attempts cluster around adding geometric constraints, with unchanged observed outcomes. This proposal instead changes how contradictory requests are negotiated: attach relation provenance to graph edges, extract an actual positive-cycle conflict when graph relaxation fails, and branch on retracting each implicated relation. Retraction removes every edge belonging to that relation, including proximity refinements. This replaces irrevocable greedy subset selection with explicit conflict-directed exploration of alternatives.

The implementation combines that new relation-selection mechanism with the previously successful support-height construction, difference constraints, collision-separation branching, and proximity rectangles. All relations remain part of candidate scoring even after retraction. Geometrically infeasible states never supply coordinates. Room and support constraints remain mandatory during search; collision choices remain branch-specific. A bounded queue search retains its best actual geometric candidate, including partially satisfied arrangements.

## Expected benefit and risk
Conflict-directed retraction may recover better compromises when relation cycles, room limits, or proximity requirements conflict, without enumerating all relation subsets in advance. This is distinct from the historical fixed greedy subset seeds and proximity-propagation refinements. The supplied successful scenes do not establish a benefit for this change.

Risks include exponential conflict branching, finite proximity-angle coverage, numerical sensitivity in cycle extraction, and search truncation. The implementation bounds generated states and expansions, uses only the standard library, and has no scene-specific identifiers or saved coordinates. # Joint XYZ search with retractable support contacts

## Complete supplied history
I reviewed all ten supplied proposal files in full, together with all fourteen source/score pairs. These include the top-level baseline, the three historical baseline directories and their initialization copies, four iter000 attempts, and two iter001 attempts. No error logs were supplied.

All eight baseline/init snapshots use the same identifier grid and parent-centered children. Their measured combined score is 0.6738452380952381, strict success is 0, support is 1.0, collision freedom is 0.9583333333333334, and relation satisfaction is 0.21666666666666667. Their source ignores relations and gives siblings identical centers: structural limitations, not execution failures.

The six evolved attempts all report combined score and strict success of 1.0 on the six supplied development scenes. Iter000/b0/00 uses difference graphs, collision branching, and proximity rectangles; b0/01 adds disk projection. Iter000/b1/00 uses centered graph solutions, projection, and greedy relation subsets; b1/01 adds circular bound propagation. Iter001/b0/00 introduces conflict-directed relation retraction; b0/01 extends retraction to support footprints and collision obligations. Their reported evaluation times are approximately 0.178, 0.202, 0.201, 0.206, 0.216, and 0.198 seconds. All are analytic AABB evaluations with Blender verification false. No evolved attempt has an observed failure requiring a bug retry.

## New mechanism
The history clusters around horizontal graph search with unchanged observed outcomes. Every evolved implementation computes heights before search; even the soft-geometry implementation can release only support footprints, leaving vertical positions fixed.

This proposal searches all three coordinates jointly. A support obligation owns its XY containment constraints and both inequalities defining its exact vertical contact. Floor contact is represented similarly for roots. Initially every support obligation is enforced. Positive-cycle conflicts can retract an entire support obligation, allowing its object and still-supported descendants to move vertically. Collision resolution branches over all six separating directions, plus the existing explicit overlap waiver. Thus a difficult horizontal packing can be replaced by a different vertical arrangement, with any lost support counted honestly by coordinate-based scoring. Support assignments themselves remain unchanged.

This combines successful conflict-directed soft-constraint search with a previously untried vertical degree of freedom. It is not another proximity refinement or a repeat of footprint-only relaxation.
